<start> obtaining syntactic parses is crucial part of many nlp pipelines <end>
<start> however most of the world languages do not have large amounts of syntactically annotated corpora available for building parsers <end>
<start> syntactic projection techniques attempt to address this issue by using parallel corpora consisting of resource poor and resource rich language pairs taking advantage of parser for the resource rich language and word alignment between the languages to project the parses onto the data for the resource poor language <end>
<start> these projection methods can suffer however when the two languages are divergent <end>
<start> in this paper we investigate the possibility of using small parallel annotated corpora to automatically detect divergent structural patterns between two languages <end>
<start> these patterns can then be used to improve structural projection algorithms allowing for better performing nlp tools for resource poor languages in particular those that may not have large amounts of annotated data necessary for traditional fully supervised methods <end>
<start> while this detection process is not exhaustive we demonstrate that common patterns of divergence can be identified automatically without prior knowledge of given language pair and the patterns can be used to improve performance of projection algorithms <end>

<start> it creates vectors for each word from wordnet <end>
<start> these vectors encapsulate general position role of given word towards all other words in the natural language <end>
<start> any list or set of such vectors contains knowledge about the context of its component within the whole language <end>
<start> such word representation can be easily applied to many analytic tasks like classification or clustering <end>
<start> the usefulness of the UNK method was demonstrated in sentiment analysis i.e. classification with transfer learning for the real amazon opinion textual dataset <end>
<start> recently variety of lstm based conditional language models lm have been applied across range of language generation tasks <end>
<start> in this work we study various model architectures and different ways to represent and aggregate the source information in an end to end neural dialogue system framework <end>
<start> method called snapshot learning is also proposed to facilitate learning from supervised sequential signals by applying companion cross entropy objective function to the conditioning vector <end>
<start> the experimental and analytical results demonstrate firstly that competition occurs between the conditioning vector and the lm and the differing architectures provide different trade offs between the two <end>
<start> secondly the discriminative power and transparency of the conditioning vector is key to providing both model interpretability and better performance <end>
<start> thirdly snapshot learning leads to consistent performance improvements independent of which architecture is used <end>

<start> modeling crisp logical regularities is crucial in semantic parsing making it difficult for neural models with no task specific prior knowledge to achieve good results <end>

<start> the task of dialog management is commonly decomposed into two sequential subtasks dialog state tracking and dialog policy learning <end>
<start> in an end to end dialog system the aim of dialog state tracking is to accurately estimate the true dialog state from noisy observations produced by the speech recognition and the natural language understanding modules <end>
<start> the state tracking task is primarily meant to support dialog policy <end>
<start> from probabilistic perspective this is achieved by maintaining posterior distribution over hidden dialog states composed of set of context dependent variables <end>
<start> once dialog policy is learned it strives to select an optimal dialog act given the estimated dialog state and defined reward function <end>
<start> this paper introduces novel method of dialog state tracking based on bilinear UNK decomposition model that provides an efficient inference schema through collective matrix factorization <end>
<start> we evaluate the proposed approach on the second dialog state tracking challenge UNK dataset and we show that the proposed tracker gives encouraging results compared to the state of the art trackers that participated in this standard benchmark <end>
<start> finally we show that the prediction schema is computationally efficient in comparison to the previous approaches <end>
<start> conventional word sense induction wsi methods usually represent each instance with discrete linguistic features or cooccurrence features and train model for each polysemous word individually <end>

<start> distantly supervised relation extraction has been widely used to find novel relational facts from plain text <end>

<start> we introduce two first order graph based dependency parsers achieving new state of the art <end>
<start> the first is consensus parser built from an ensemble of independently trained greedy lstm transition based parsers with different random initializations <end>

<start> sentence is basic linguistic unit however little is known about how information content is distributed across different positions of sentence <end>
<start> based on authentic language data of english the present study calculated the entropy and other entropy related statistics for different sentence positions <end>
<start> the statistics indicate three step UNK shaped distribution pattern with entropy in the initial position lower than the medial positions positions other than the initial and final the medial positions lower than the final position and the medial positions showing no significant difference <end>
<start> the results suggest that the hypotheses of constant entropy rate and uniform information density do not hold for the sentence medial positions the context of word in sentence should not be simply defined as all the words preceding it in the same sentence and the contextual information content in sentence does not accumulate incrementally but follows pattern of the whole is greater than the sum of parts <end>
<start> neural machine translation nmt heavily relies on word level modelling to learn semantic representations of input sentences <end>

<start> to handle these issues we propose word lattice based recurrent neural network rnn encoders for nmt which generalize the standard rnn to word lattice topology <end>

<start> formal semantics and distributional semantics are two important semantic frameworks in natural language processing nlp <end>
<start> cognitive semantics belongs to the movement of cognitive linguistics which is based on contemporary cognitive science <end>
<start> each framework could deal with some meaning phenomena but none of them fulfills all requirements proposed by applications <end>
<start> unified semantic theory characterizing all important language phenomena has both theoretical and practical significance however although many attempts have been made in recent years no existing theory has achieved this goal yet <end>
<start> this article introduces new semantic theory that has the potential to characterize most of the important meaning phenomena of natural language and to fulfill most of the necessary requirements for philosophical analysis and for nlp applications <end>
<start> the theory is based on unified representation of information and constructs kind of mathematical model called cognitive model to interpret natural language expressions in compositional manner <end>
<start> it accepts the empirical assumption of cognitive semantics and overcomes most shortcomings of formal semantics and of distributional semantics <end>
<start> the theory however is not simple combination of existing theories but an extensive generalization of classic logic and formal semantics <end>
<start> it inherits nearly all advantages of formal semantics and also provides descriptive contents for objects and events as fine gram as possible descriptive contents which represent the results of human cognition <end>

<start> computational model of the construction of word meaning through exposure to texts is built in order to simulate the effects of co occurrence values on word semantic similarities paragraph by paragraph <end>
<start> semantic similarity is here viewed as association <end>
<start> it turns out that the similarity between two words w1 and w2 strongly increases with co occurrence decreases with the occurrence of w1 without w2 or w2 without w1 and slightly increases with high order co occurrences <end>

<start> this paper describes probabilistic top down parser for minimalist grammars <end>

<start> this is due to the long tailed distribution of valid corrections for sentence <end>
<start> concretely we show that lcb incentivizes gec systems to avoid correcting even when they can generate valid correction <end>
<start> consequently existing systems obtain comparable or superior performance compared to humans by making few but targeted changes to the input <end>
<start> similar effects on text simplification further support our claims <end>
<start> text generation is crucial task in nlp <end>
<start> recently several adversarial generative models have been proposed to improve the exposure bias problem in text generation <end>
<start> though these models gain great success they still suffer from the problems of reward sparsity and mode collapse <end>
<start> in order to address these two problems in this paper we employ inverse reinforcement learning irl for text generation <end>
<start> specifically the irl framework learns reward function on training data and then an optimal policy to maximum the expected total reward <end>
<start> similar to the adversarial models the reward and policy function in irl are optimized alternately <end>
<start> our method has two advantages the reward function can produce more dense reward signals <end>
<start> the generation policy trained by entropy regularized policy gradient encourages to generate more diversified texts <end>
<start> experiment results demonstrate that our proposed method can generate higher quality texts than the previous methods <end>

<start> systematic compositionality is the ability to recombine meaningful units with regular and predictable outcomes and it seen as key to humans capacity for generalization in language <end>
<start> recent work has studied systematic compositionality in modern seq2seq models using generalization to novel navigation instructions in grounded environment as probing tool requiring models to quickly bootstrap the meaning of new words <end>
<start> we extend this framework here to settings where the model needs only to recombine well trained functional words such as around and right in novel contexts <end>
<start> our findings confirm and strengthen the earlier ones seq2seq models can be impressively good at generalizing to novel combinations of previously seen input but only when they receive extensive training on the specific pattern to be generalized e.g. generalizing from many examples of around right to jump around right while failing when generalization requires novel application of compositional rules e.g. inferring the meaning of around right from those of right and around <end>

<start> recurrent neural networks rnns have been proven to be effective in modeling sequential data and they have been applied to boost variety of tasks such as document classification speech recognition and machine translation <end>
<start> most of existing rnn models have been designed for sequences assumed to be identically and independently distributed i.i.d <end>
<start> however in many real world applications sequences are naturally linked <end>
<start> for example web documents are connected by hyperlinks and genes interact with each other <end>
<start> on the one hand linked sequences are inherently not i.i.d <end>
<start> which poses tremendous challenges to existing rnn models <end>
<start> on the other hand linked sequences offer link information in addition to the sequential information which enables unprecedented opportunities to build advanced rnn models <end>
<start> in this paper we study the problem of rnn for linked sequences <end>
<start> in particular we introduce principled approach to capture link information and propose linked recurrent neural network UNK which models sequential and link information coherently <end>
<start> we conduct experiments on real world datasets from multiple domains and the experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework <end>

<start> the encoder decoder is the typical framework for neural machine translation nmt and different structures have been developed for improving the translation performance <end>
<start> transformer is one of the most promising structures which can leverage the self attention mechanism to capture the semantic dependency from global view <end>
<start> however it can not distinguish the relative position of different tokens very well such as the tokens located at the left or right of the current token and can not focus on the local information around the current token either <end>
<start> to alleviate these problems we propose novel attention mechanism named hybrid self attention network UNK which accommodates some specific designed masks for self attention network to extract various semantic such as the global local information the left right part context <end>
<start> finally squeeze gate is introduced to combine different kinds of sans for fusion <end>
<start> experimental results on three machine translation tasks show that our proposed framework outperforms the transformer baseline significantly and achieves superior results over state of the art nmt systems <end>
<start> current neural machine translation nmt employs language specific encoder to represent the source sentence and adopts language specific decoder to generate target translation <end>
<start> this language dependent design leads to large scale network parameters and makes the duality of the parallel data UNK <end>

<start> we propose instead to measure bias using the direct normalized co occurrence associations between the word and the representative concept words first order measure by reconstructing the co occurrence estimates inherent in the word embedding models <end>
<start> to study our novel corpus bias measurement method we calculate the correlation of the gender bias values estimated from the text to the actual gender bias statistics of the u.s. job market provided by two recent collections <end>

<start> transfer learning aims to solve the data sparsity for target domain by applying information of the source domain <end>

<start> in this paper we address the problem of effectively self training neural networks in low resource setting <end>
<start> self training is frequently used to automatically increase the amount of training data <end>
<start> however in low resource scenario it is less effective due to unreliable annotations created using self labeling of unlabeled data <end>
<start> we propose to combine self training with noise handling on the self labeled data <end>
<start> directly estimating noise on the combined clean training set and self labeled data can lead to corruption of the clean data and hence performs worse <end>

<start> in our experiments on chunking and ner this approach performs more robustly than the baselines <end>
<start> complementary to this explicit approach noise can also be handled implicitly with the help of an auxiliary learning task <end>

<start> we introduce novel parser for minimalist grammars mg encoded as system of first order logic formulae that may be evaluated using an smt solver and novel procedure for inferring minimalist grammars using this parser <end>
<start> the input to this procedure is sequence of sentences that have been annotated with syntactic relations such as semantic role labels connecting arguments to predicates and subject verb agreement <end>
<start> the output of this procedure is set of minimalist grammars each of which is able to parse the sentences in the input sequence such that the parse for sentence has the same syntactic relations as those specified in the annotation for that sentence <end>
<start> we applied this procedure to set of sentences annotated with syntactic relations and evaluated the inferred grammars using cost functions inspired by the minimum description length principle and the subset principle <end>

<start> while data augmentation is an important trick to boost the accuracy of deep learning methods in computer vision tasks its study in natural language tasks is still very limited <end>

<start> different from previous augmentation methods that randomly drop swap or replace words with other words in sentence we softly augment randomly chosen word in sentence by its contextual mixture of multiple related words <end>

<start> answer selection is an important subtask of question answering qa where deep models usually achieve better performance <end>
<start> most deep models adopt question answer interaction mechanisms such as attention to get vector representations for answers <end>

<start> this procedure is time consuming for deep models with complex encoders like bert which usually have better accuracy than simple encoders <end>

<start> in this paper we aim at tackling general issue in nlp tasks where some of the negative examples are highly similar to the positive examples i.e. hard negative examples <end>
<start> we propose the distant supervision as regularizer UNK approach to tackle this issue <end>
<start> the original task is converted to multi task learning problem in which distant supervision is used to retrieve hard negative examples <end>
<start> the obtained hard negative examples are then used as regularizer <end>
<start> the original target objective of distinguishing positive examples from negative examples is jointly optimized with the auxiliary task objective of distinguishing softened positive i.e. hard negative examples plus positive examples from easy negative examples <end>
<start> in the neural context this can be done by outputting the same representation from the last neural layer to different UNK functions <end>
<start> using this strategy we can improve the performance of baseline models in range of different nlp tasks including text classification sequence labeling and reading comprehension <end>

<start> first the document explorer iteratively selects relevant documents and represents divergent reasoning chains in tree structure so as to allow UNK information from all chains <end>
<start> the answer UNK then proposes an answer from every root to leaf path in the reasoning tree <end>
<start> finally the evidence UNK extracts key sentence containing the proposed answer from every path and combines them to predict the final answer <end>
<start> intuitively epar approximates the coarse to fine grained comprehension behavior of human readers when facing multiple long documents <end>
<start> we jointly optimize our modules by minimizing the sum of losses from each stage conditioned on the previous stage output <end>
<start> on two multi hop reading comprehension datasets wikihop and UNK our epar model achieves significant improvements over the baseline and competitive results compared to the state of the art model <end>

<start> multilingual acoustic models have been successfully applied to low resource speech recognition <end>

<start> the model is eventually fine tuned on each target corpus <end>
<start> this approach however fails to exploit the relatedness and similarity among corpora in the training set <end>
<start> for example the target corpus might benefit more from corpus in the same domain or corpus from close language <end>
<start> in this work we propose simple but useful sampling strategy to take advantage of this relatedness <end>

<start> this paper proposes novel procedure for training an encoder decoder based deep neural network which compresses nxm models into single model enabling us to dynamically choose the number of encoder and decoder layers for decoding <end>
<start> usually the output of the last layer of the layer encoder is fed to the layer decoder and the output of the last decoder layer is used to compute softmax loss <end>
<start> instead our method computes single loss consisting of nxm losses the softmax loss for the output of each of the decoder layers derived using the output of each of the encoder layers <end>
<start> single model trained by our method can be used for decoding with an arbitrary fewer number of encoder and decoder layers <end>

<start> variational language models seek to estimate the posterior of latent variables with an approximated variational posterior <end>
<start> the model often assumes the variational posterior to be factorized even when the true posterior is not <end>
<start> the learned variational posterior under this assumption does not capture the dependency relationships over latent variables <end>
<start> we argue that this would cause typical training problem called posterior collapse observed in all other variational language models <end>
<start> we propose gaussian copula variational autoencoder vae to avert this problem <end>
<start> copula is widely used to model correlation and dependencies of high dimensional random variables and therefore it is helpful to maintain the dependency relationships that are lost in vae <end>
<start> the empirical results show that by modeling the correlation of latent variables explicitly using neural parametric copula we can avert this training difficulty while getting competitive results among all other vae approaches <end>

<start> we consider the zero shot entity linking challenge where each entity is defined by short textual description and the model must read these descriptions together with the mention context to make the final linking decisions <end>

<start> in this paper we introduce simple and effective two stage approach for zero shot linking based on fine tuned bert architectures <end>

<start> empirical research in natural language processing nlp has adopted narrow set of principles for assessing hypotheses relying mainly on value computation which suffers from several known issues <end>

<start> we address this gap by contrasting various hypothesis assessment techniques especially those not commonly used in the field such as evaluations based on bayesian inference <end>
<start> since these statistical techniques differ in the hypotheses they can support we argue that practitioners should first decide their target hypothesis before choosing an assessment method <end>
<start> this is crucial because common fallacies misconceptions and UNK surrounding hypothesis assessment methods often stem from discrepancy between what one would like to claim versus what the method used actually assesses <end>
<start> our survey reveals that these issues are omnipresent in the nlp research community <end>
<start> as step forward we provide best practices and guidelines tailored to nlp research as well as an easy to use package called UNK for bayesian assessment of hypotheses complementing existing tools <end>

<start> this paper proposes an utterance to utterance interactive matching network UNK imn for multi turn response selection in retrieval based chatbots <end>
<start> different from previous methods following context to response matching or utterance to response matching frameworks this model treats both contexts and responses as sequences of utterances when calculating the matching degrees between them <end>
<start> for context response pair the UNK imn model first encodes each utterance separately using recurrent and self attention layers <end>

<start> the distances between context and response utterances are employed as prior component when calculating the attention weights <end>
<start> finally sentence level aggregation and context response level aggregation are executed in turn to obtain the feature vector for matching degree prediction <end>

<start> relation tuple consists of two entities and the relation between them and often such tuples are found in unstructured text <end>

<start> extracting such relation tuples from sentence is difficult task and sharing of entities or overlapping entities among the tuples makes it more challenging <end>

<start> in this paper we propose two approaches to use encoder decoder architecture for jointly extracting entities and relations <end>

<start> next we propose pointer network based decoding approach where an entire tuple is generated at every time step <end>

<start> conversations have an intrinsic one to many property which means that multiple responses can be appropriate for the same dialog context <end>
<start> in task oriented dialogs this property leads to different valid dialog policies towards task completion <end>
<start> however none of the existing task oriented dialog generation approaches takes this property into account <end>
<start> we propose multi action data augmentation UNK framework to utilize the one to many property to generate diverse appropriate dialog responses <end>
<start> specifically we first use dialog states to summarize the dialog history and then discover all possible mappings from every dialog state to its different valid system actions <end>
<start> during dialog system training we enable the current dialog state to map to all valid system actions discovered in the previous process to create additional state action pairs <end>
<start> by incorporating these additional pairs the dialog policy learns balanced action distribution which further guides the dialog model to generate diverse responses <end>
<start> experimental results show that the proposed framework consistently improves dialog policy diversity and results in improved response diversity and appropriateness <end>

<start> the frequencies at which individual words occur across languages follow power law distributions pattern of findings known as zipf law <end>

<start> the task of text classification is usually divided into two stages \it text feature extraction and \it classification <end>

<start> we propose and evaluate novel procedure for training multiple transformers with tied parameters which compresses multiple models into one enabling the dynamic choice of the number of encoder and decoder layers during decoding <end>
<start> in sequence to sequence modeling typically the output of the last layer of the layer encoder is fed to the layer decoder and the output of the last decoder layer is used to compute loss <end>
<start> instead our method computes single loss consisting of nxm losses where each loss is computed from the output of one of the decoder layers connected to one of the encoder layers <end>

<start> existing neural machine translation nmt systems utilize sequence to sequence neural networks to generate target translation word by word and then make the generated word at each time step and the counterpart in the references as consistent as possible <end>
<start> however the trained translation model tends to focus on ensuring the accuracy of the generated target word at the current time step and does not consider its future cost which means the expected cost of generating the subsequent target translation i.e. the next target word <end>
<start> to respond to this issue we propose simple and effective method to model the future cost of each target word for nmt systems <end>
<start> in detail time dependent future cost is estimated based on the current generated target word and its contextual information to boost the training of the nmt model <end>
<start> furthermore the learned future context representation at the current time step is used to help the generation of the next target word in the decoding <end>

<start> recently variational auto encoder vae based approaches have made impressive progress on improving the diversity of generated responses <end>

<start> however how to find suitable estimation for such hardness then explicitly modeling adaptive computation depths are still not investigated <end>
<start> in this paper we try to solve this issue and propose two effective approaches namely mutual information based estimation and reconstruction loss based estimation to measure the hardness of learning the representation for word and determine its computational depth <end>
<start> results on the classic text classification task datasets in various sizes and domains show that our approaches achieve superior performance while preserving higher efficiency in computation over the vanilla transformer and previous depth adaptive models <end>
<start> more importantly our approaches lead to more robust depth adaptive transformer models with better interpretability of the depth distribution <end>

<start> recently the olid dataset used at semeval-2019 proposed hierarchical three level annotation taxonomy which addresses different types of offensive language as well as important information such as the target of such content <end>
<start> the categorization provides meaningful and important information for understanding offensive language <end>
<start> however the olid dataset is limited in size especially for some of the low level categories which included only few hundred instances thus making it challenging to train robust deep learning models <end>
<start> here we address this limitation by creating the largest available dataset for this task solid <end>
<start> solid contains over nine million english tweets labeled in semi supervised manner <end>
<start> we further demonstrate experimentally that using solid along with olid yields improved performance on the olid test set for two different models especially for the lower levels of the taxonomy <end>
<start> finally we perform analysis of the models performance on easy and hard examples of offensive language using data annotated in semi supervised way <end>
<start> humor plays an important role in human languages and it is essential to model humor when building intelligence systems <end>
<start> among different forms of humor puns perform wordplay for humorous effects by employing words with double UNK and high phonetic similarity <end>
<start> however identifying and modeling puns are challenging as puns usually involved implicit semantic or phonological tricks <end>
<start> in this paper we propose pronunciation attentive contextualized pun recognition pcpr to perceive human humor detect if sentence contains puns and locate them in the sentence <end>
<start> pcpr derives contextualized representation for each word in sentence by capturing the association between the surrounding context and its corresponding phonetic symbols <end>
<start> extensive experiments are conducted on two benchmark datasets <end>
<start> results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly outperforms the state of the art methods in pun detection and location tasks <end>
<start> in depth analyses verify the effectiveness and robustness of pcpr <end>
<start> the success of pretrained contextual encoders such as elmo and bert has brought great deal of interest in what these models learn do they without explicit supervision learn to encode meaningful notions of linguistic structure <end>
<start> if so how is this structure encoded <end>
<start> to investigate this we introduce latent subclass learning UNK modification to existing classifier based probing methods that induces latent categorization or ontology of the probe inputs <end>
<start> without access to fine grained gold labels UNK extracts emergent structure from input representations in an interpretable and quantifiable form <end>
<start> in experiments we find strong evidence of familiar categories such as notion of UNK in elmo as well as novel ontological distinctions such as preference for fine grained semantic roles on core arguments <end>
<start> our results provide unique new evidence of emergent structure in pretrained encoders including departures from existing annotations which are inaccessible to earlier methods <end>
<start> interpretable rationales for model predictions play critical role in practical applications <end>
<start> in this study we develop models possessing interpretable inference process for structured prediction <end>
<start> specifically we present method of instance based learning that learns similarities between spans <end>
<start> at inference time each span is assigned class label based on its similar spans in the training set where it is easy to understand how much each training instance contributes to the predictions <end>
<start> through empirical analysis on named entity recognition we demonstrate that our method enables to build models that have high interpretability without sacrificing performance <end>
<start> we present novel supervised word alignment method based on cross language span prediction <end>
<start> we first formalize word alignment problem as collection of independent predictions from token in the source sentence to span in the target sentence <end>
<start> as this is equivalent to squad v2.0 style question answering task we then solve this problem by using multilingual bert which is fine tuned on manually created gold word alignment data <end>
<start> we greatly improved the word alignment accuracy by adding the context of the token to the question <end>
<start> in the experiments using five word alignment datasets among chinese japanese german romanian french and english we show that the proposed method significantly outperformed previous supervised and unsupervised word alignment methods without using any bitexts for pretraining <end>
<start> for example we achieved an f1 score of for the chinese english data which is points higher than the previous state of the art supervised methods <end>
<start> in this paper we propose method to extract bilingual texts automatically from noisy parallel corpora by framing the problem as token level span prediction such as squad style reading comprehension <end>
<start> to extract span of the target document that is translation of given source sentence span we use either qanet or multilingual bert <end>
<start> qanet can be trained for specific parallel corpus from scratch while multilingual bert can utilize pre trained multilingual representations <end>
<start> for the span prediction method using qanet we introduce total optimization method using integer linear programming to achieve consistency in the predicted parallel spans <end>
<start> we conduct parallel sentence extraction experiment using simulated noisy parallel corpora with two language pairs en fr and en ja and find that the proposed method using qanet achieves significantly better accuracy than baseline method using two bi directional rnn encoders particularly for distant language pairs en ja <end>
<start> we also conduct sentence alignment experiment using en ja newspaper articles and find that the proposed method using multilingual bert achieves significantly better accuracy than baseline method using bilingual dictionary and dynamic programming <end>

<start> the challenges of building knowledge grounded retrieval based chatbots lie in how to ground conversation on the background knowledge and how to perform their matching with the response <end>

<start> aspect classification identifying aspects of text segments facilitates numerous applications such as sentiment analysis and review summarization <end>
<start> to alleviate the human effort on annotating massive texts in this paper we study the problem of classifying aspects based on only few user provided seed words for pre defined aspects <end>

<start> even domain experts have difficulties to UNK seed words for the misc aspect making existing seed driven text classification methods not applicable <end>
<start> we propose novel framework UNK which enables mutual enhancements between pre defined aspects and the misc aspect via iterative classifier training and seed updating <end>
<start> specifically it trains classifier for pre defined aspects and then leverages it to induce the supervision for the misc aspect <end>

<start> neural language models are usually trained to match the distributional properties of large scale corpus by minimizing the log loss <end>
<start> while straightforward to optimize this approach forces the model to reproduce all variations in the dataset including noisy and invalid references e.g. UNK and UNK facts <end>
<start> worse the commonly used log loss is overly sensitive to such phenomena and even small fraction of noisy data can degrade performance <end>
<start> in this work we show that the distinguishability of the models and reference serves as principled and robust alternative for handling invalid references <end>
<start> to optimize distinguishability we propose loss truncation which adaptively removes high loss examples during training <end>
<start> we show this is as easy to optimize as log loss and tightly bounds distinguishability under noise <end>
<start> empirically we demonstrate that loss truncation outperforms existing baselines on distinguishability on summarization task and show that samples generated by the loss truncation model have factual accuracy ratings that exceed those of baselines and match human references <end>

<start> many extractive question answering models are trained to predict start and end positions of answers <end>
<start> the choice of predicting answers as positions is mainly due to its simplicity and effectiveness <end>

<start> to safely deliver position information without position bias we train models with various de biasing methods including entropy regularization and bias ensembling <end>

<start> transformer UNK benefits from its key design of the multi head self attention network san which extracts information from various perspectives through transforming the given input into different subspaces <end>
<start> however its simple linear transformation aggregation strategy may still potentially fail to fully capture deeper contextualized information <end>
<start> in this paper we thus propose the capsule transformer which extends the linear transformation into more general capsule routing algorithm by taking san as special case of capsule network <end>
<start> so that the resulted capsule transformer is capable of obtaining better attention distribution representation of the input sequence via information aggregation among different heads and words <end>
<start> specifically we see groups of attention weights in san as low layer capsules <end>
<start> by applying the iterative capsule routing algorithm they can be further aggregated into high layer capsules which contain deeper contextualized information <end>
<start> experimental results on the widely used machine translation datasets show our proposed capsule transformer outperforms strong transformer baseline significantly <end>

<start> neural machine translation nmt models do not work well in domains different from the training data <end>
<start> the standard approach to this problem is to build small parallel data in the target domain and perform domain adaptation from source domain where massive parallel data is available <end>
<start> however domain adaptation between distant domains e.g. subtitles and research papers does not perform effectively because of mismatches in vocabulary it will encounter many domain specific unknown words e.g. UNK and words whose meanings shift across domains e.g. UNK <end>
<start> in this study aiming to solve these vocabulary mismatches in distant domain adaptation we propose vocabulary adaptation simple method for effective fine tuning that adapts embedding layers in given pre trained nmt model to the target domain <end>
<start> prior to fine tuning our method replaces word embeddings in embedding layers of the nmt model by projecting general word embeddings induced from monolingual data in the target domain onto the source domain embedding space <end>
<start> experimental results on distant domain adaptation for english to japanese translation and german to english translation indicate that our vocabulary adaptation improves the performance of fine tuning by bleu points <end>
<start> despite its original goal to jointly learn to align and translate prior researches suggest that the state of the art neural machine translation model transformer captures poor word alignment through its attention mechanism <end>
<start> in this paper we show that attention weights do capture accurate word alignment which could only be revealed if we choose the correct decoding step and layer to induce word alignment <end>
